categories.title: HTML & CSS
categories.card_description: Real pages and real layouts: the box model, float, positioning, Flexbox, animations, and responsive design.
categories.intro: Eight tutorials, meant to be worked through roughly in order. Together they take you from a single styled page to a complete, responsive, multi-column site shell, using nothing but HTML and CSS — no framework, no build step, just files you can open directly in a browser. Each one builds on ideas from the ones before it, so later tutorials will point back to earlier ones ("Prerequisites: ...") rather than re-explaining a technique from scratch.

tutorials.title: Your First HTML + CSS Page
tutorials.summary: Combining HTML structure and CSS (colors, the box model, centering, hover transitions) into one complete, real page.

tutorials.title: Layout Designing with div, span, and Float
tutorials.summary: `<div>`/`<span>`, `id` vs. `class`, and building a header + nav menu + three-column layout + footer with `float`, `width`, and `overflow`.

tutorials.title: CSS Positioning
tutorials.summary: `static`/`relative`/`absolute`/`fixed`/`sticky`, `z-index` and stacking, and real patterns like tooltips and a centered modal.

tutorials.title: Flexbox Layout
tutorials.summary: `display: flex`, both axes, `flex-direction`, `justify-content`, `align-items`, `flex-wrap`, `gap`, `flex-grow`/`shrink`/`basis`, `align-self`, and real navbar/centering patterns.

tutorials.title: Multilevel Navigation with Positioning
tutorials.summary: Building a dropdown menu from scratch: a single-level bar, then a second-level dropdown with `relative`/`absolute`, then a guided challenge to add a third-level flyout yourself.

tutorials.title: Complete Page Layout with Float and Positioning
tutorials.summary: Combining both tutorials above into one real page: a sticky toolbar, a vertical sidebar menu, a floated three-column body, a floated four-column footer, and a fixed "back to top" button.

tutorials.title: CSS Transitions and Animations
tutorials.summary: `transition` properties and timing functions, `@keyframes`, `animation` properties, a spinner, a pulsing badge, a fade-in entrance, plus performance and accessibility notes.

tutorials.title: Responsive Web Design
tutorials.summary: The viewport tag, mobile-first design, media queries, responsive units, `clamp()`, responsive images, and a complete responsive three-card layout.

categories.title: JavaScript
categories.card_description: The language itself: closures and scope, modules, `this`, and patterns you'll lean on in Express and React.
categories.intro: Tool-focused tutorials on the JavaScript language itself — beyond what's already covered in the [Web Technologies](../../web-technologies/index.md) book chapters on core JavaScript, array methods, and async/await. Think deeper dives and standalone projects: closures and scope, the module system, working with `this`, and patterns you'll lean on constantly once you get to Express and React.

categories.title: Express
categories.card_description: Routing, middleware, request/response handling, and connecting to MongoDB with Node's most-used web framework.
categories.intro: Hands-on tutorials for Express.js, the "E" in MERN: routing, middleware, request/response handling, connecting to MongoDB, and structuring a real API — building on the server-side chapters already in the [Web Technologies](../../web-technologies/index.md) book, but as standalone, project-based walkthroughs.

categories.intro: Hands-on tutorials for React, the "R" in MERN: components and props, hooks and state, routing, and talking to a real API — building on the front-end chapters already in the [Web Technologies](../../web-technologies/index.md) and [Advanced Web Technologies](../../advanced-web-technologies/index.md) books, but as standalone, project-based walkthroughs.

categories.title: DevOps
categories.card_description: Environment setup, Git and GitHub, version control fundamentals, and this course's own submission workflow.
categories.intro: Everything here is tooling and workflow rather than a language or framework: getting your machine ready for MERN-stack work, and the version control every project in this course is built and submitted through. Start with environment setup if your machine isn't ready yet, then Git and GitHub if version control is new to you, then the submission workflow regardless of your Git experience — it covers this course's specific repository structure and what counts as a valid, on-time submission.

tutorials.title: MERN Environment Setup
tutorials.summary: Installing VS Code (and essential extensions), Node.js/npm, nodemon, MongoDB (Atlas or local), and Git/GitHub Desktop.

tutorials.title: Git and GitHub
tutorials.summary: Version control fundamentals, everyday Git commands, branching and merging, undoing mistakes, collaborating on GitHub with forks and pull requests, and GitHub Desktop / GUI alternatives.

tutorials.title: Submitting Coursework via GitHub
tutorials.summary: This course's actual submission workflow: one repository, a required folder structure, and what counts as an on-time, valid submission.
